h: Planning a Proper West Yorkshire Day Out
p: With so much going on at Xscape, it pays to have a plan. Decide which activities matter most to your group, book them ahead and space them out so there's time for food in between. Trying to rush from snow slope to games to cinema in one afternoon sounds great on paper, but tired kids and hungry adults soon put a stop to that. A couple of highlights done properly beats ten things done in a hurry.

If you're bringing a mixed-age group, check any age or height rules for the activities you're interested in, and remember that evenings may be geared more towards older visitors. Comfortable shoes are a good idea, as you'll probably be on your feet for much of the day.

Once you've had your fill of indoor fun, West Yorkshire has some great places to explore nearby. RSPB Fairburn Ings is just outside Castleford, with easy trails and hides for spotting birds on the lakes. Over in Wakefield, The Hepworth Wakefield is a striking riverside gallery devoted to modern art and sculptor Barbara Hepworth, and the Yorkshire Sculpture Park near West Bretton has large-scale artworks set across rolling parkland.

History lovers can head to Nostell, a grand Georgian house run by the National Trust near Wakefield, with parkland and gardens to wander. Back in Castleford itself, the Castleford Tigers rugby league side bring a real buzz to town on match days, so check the fixtures if you're planning to drive in.
